correctness.rationale: The exact real ell1 norming-functional criterion gives x⊥B y iff |sum_{i in supp(x)}sign(x_i)y_i| ≤ sum_{i outside supp(x)}|y_i|, valid also at zeros. For a mutual clique containing an axis, reverse orthogonality forces others into its orthogonal two-coordinate plane, where at most two lines coexist (clique <=3). For a given two-coordinate support, a mutual pair forces both vectors to have equal absolute nonzero coordinates with opposite relative signs; at most the two diagonal projective lines. Three full-support clique vectors cannot exist because sign-functional equations force one of three nonzero coordinates to vanish; with any full-support line, there are ≤2 full-support and ≤1 for each of three pair supports, total ≤5. Therefore max 6, and equality forces exactly the unique six diagonals across three pair supports. Independent exact evaluation of all 15 pairs of those six candidates confirmed bidirectional inequality. The finite projective-coordinate-grid CHECK.py was examined (49 lines in dimension three), but the all-real infinite claim rests on the symbolic support proof, not grid exhaustion.
residual_risks: Finite experimental corroboration does not substitute for infinite claim, unless exhaustive finite reduction independently justified.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS with named survey coverage risk. Arambašić–Guterman–Kuzma–Rajić–Zhilina 2021 symmetrized orthogonality graph gives general dimension bounds and graph framework; Wang–Ji–Wei 2023 one-sided/mutual distinctions and an ell1^3 one-sided example do not provide the sharp mutual projective clique number SIX with UNIQUE extremizer. The published Resultary n-general exponential lower-bound construction is an existential bound without the matching exact upper bound and rigidity at n=3. Nearby ell_infinity ternary cliques are not transferable by duality: mutual BJ orthogonality is not preserved by replacing a Banach norm by its dual. Available searches found no stronger explicit covering classification.
